summary.headline: Ajmera Realty FY26 presales hit record INR 1,701 Cr (+57% YoY), beating INR 1,600 Cr guidance; FY27 presales target set at INR 2,200 Cr.
summary.overview: FY26 was a record year for Ajmera Realty: presales of INR 1,701 Cr (+57% YoY), collections of INR 1,103 Cr (+71%), and total sales revenue of INR 1,098 Cr (+46%). EBITDA rose 25% to INR 306 Cr and PAT rose 24% to INR 157 Cr. Debt-to-equity fell to 0.53x against an annual guidance of 0.85x. Management guided FY27 presales to about INR 2,200 Cr and debt-to-equity to 1.00x, citing the Kanjurmarg land conversion, a planned INR 1,800 Cr of business development, and eight launches. Most Q&A focused on the Kanjurmarg conversion timeline, Versova luxury sales pace, Manhattan pricing, and the reason for the higher gearing guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs annual guidance of 0.85x; 1.13x in FY21

financial_highlights.value: INR 25,770 per sq ft in FY26

segments.name: Wadala (Manhattan 1 & 2, Greenfinity)
segments.commentary: Manhattan 1 about 90% sold with RCC done in Towers A and B. Manhattan 2 (launched FY26) about 48% sold. Average sales price about INR 37,000/sq ft in Manhattan 1 and INR 35,000/sq ft in Manhattan 2 last quarter. Greenfinity next phase 94% sold, OC expected soon.

segments.name: Bandra (33Fifteen, commercial)
segments.commentary: Commercial launch about 17% of inventory sold.

segments.name: Versova (Vann by Ajmera)
segments.commentary: Premium luxury project launched in Q4 FY26; average carpet area about 1,700-1,800 sq ft. Sales slow at launch by design; management expects steady, not one-shot, sales. Only 3 units sold in the last month of FY26 per Q&A.

segments.name: Bhandup (Ajmera Vihara)
segments.commentary: 81% sold; 21st floor slab cast in rehab building, 4th floor slab cast in sale building.

segments.name: Bengaluru (Iris, Marina)
segments.commentary: Iris about 88% sold; Marina (launched Q4 FY25) 69% sold, first floor slab in progress.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales target about INR 2,200 Cr.
FY27 launch pipeline about INR 6,324 Cr GDV; total GDV to be monetised about INR 19,518 Cr including Wadala land bank GDV of INR 13,194 Cr.
Revenue visibility INR 10,432 Cr: INR 4,108 Cr from existing projects (INR 1,837 Cr committed sales, INR 2,270 Cr unsold inventory) plus INR 6,324 Cr upcoming launches.
Net cash flow (pre-tax) from OC-received and ongoing portfolio estimated at about INR 3,150 Cr; launch pipeline expected to generate about INR 1,400 Cr+ cash.

Debt-to-equity guidance raised to 1.00x for FY27 (from 0.53x actual), reflecting Kanjurmarg conversion, INR 1,800 Cr of new business development and eight FY27 launches; management says this is conservative and SPV-level funding is being pursued.
Business development target INR 1,500-1,800 Cr in FY27; Manhattan pricing to rise at least 10-15% YoY.
Boutique offices (Wadala) and Borivali redevelopment both targeted for Q3 FY27; Manhattan 3 in FY27 launches.
capex_capacity: Kanjurmarg 11-acre land: conversion from leasehold to freehold applied for; management hopes to resolve in about the next quarter. Launch targeted in H2 FY27 or later, 3-4 months after regulatory clearances; may also pursue monetisation.
Kanjurmarg: master planner appointed, master planning complete, police housing construction started, IOD and environment clearances in parallel.
Kanjurmarg plan is a combined residential, commercial and retail launch in one go; funding talks at SPV level with funds, described as near tie-up.
Property, plant and equipment rose from about INR 35 Cr to INR 60+ Cr, mainly capitalisation of Mivan shuttering across multiple projects.
Management said a 7-acre Kanjurmarg land outright sale has been discussed but not finalised; no price or timeline disclosed.
demand_pricing: Unsold inventory about INR 2,200 Cr as of March 2026, across OC-completed and ongoing projects.
Committed sales about INR 1,850 Cr (INR 1,800 Cr on ongoing projects pending revenue plus about INR 40 Cr on OC-received projects).
Revenue is recognised only after 25% construction completion and collections above 10%, per project.

Manhattan pricing: management targets at least 10-15% YoY price increases; claims 8-10% premium over the last few years due to township amenities. Says it is the only player in its micro market offering such amenities at this scale.
Competition: Raymond's nearby project was cited by an analyst as selling faster; management said Manhattan 2 sold over 40% (about INR 700 Cr) in 15-20 days at launch.
Near-term demand: buyers more cautious on geopolitics; purchase-to-closure cycle stretched from 30-45 days to 40-60 days, though demand remains good.
Management says AI is affecting work efficiency rather than housing demand.
Vann (Versova) is a luxury product; management expects slow initial sales that pick up over the project life.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Kanjurmarg 11-acre project launch, and why switch from leasehold to freehold?
qa_highlights.answer: Conversion is applied for and expected to be resolved in about a quarter; launch targeted H2 FY27 after IOD and environment clearances. Management said customers are more comfortable with freehold, though leasehold launch is possible.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for Wadala boutique offices and Manhattan 3, and Borivali?
qa_highlights.answer: Boutique offices and Borivali redevelopment both targeted for Q3 FY27; Manhattan 3 is part of FY27 launches.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Versova (Vann) sell slowly at launch?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a luxury product where slow velocity was expected; sales will come steadily over the project life. Bandra and Solis were launched earlier and have performed well.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin be sustained, and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the INR 6,324 Cr launch pipeline and about INR 1,400 Cr+ cash generation as support for sustainable margins; no separate capex figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt-to-equity guidance rising to 1.0x if Kanjurmarg will be funded at SPV level?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance includes Kanjurmarg conversion, eight FY27 launches and conservative assumptions; SPV-level funding is being pursued to keep it off the listed company.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7-acre Kanjurmarg land being sold outright?
qa_highlights.answer: Offers are under discussion but nothing is finalised; no price or timeline given. Company will update when narrowed down.

risks_watch: Kanjurmarg conversion and IOD/environment approvals; launch slip risk beyond H2 FY27.
Gearing rising from 0.53x to 1.00x guidance; dependence on SPV-level funding not yet closed.
Management says FY27 presales of INR 2,200 Cr and revenue visibility rely on execution and on launch timing for INR 6,324 Cr of new projects.
Slow sales at Versova (Vann) and Bandra commercial (17% sold); Manhattan pricing growth of 10-15% YoY vs competition (Raymond).
Longer buyer decision cycles due to geopolitical caution; construction cost escalation noted by management.
Possible outright sale of the Kanjurmarg land; no terms disclosed.
Management did not explain the PPE explanation fully (said to be mainly Mivan shuttering capitalisation).
summary.management_tone: Confident on sales, collections and deleveraging, but measured on FY27, which management described as a "calibrated" year focused on disciplined execution. Answers on Kanjurmarg conversion timing and the Kanjurmarg land sale were hedged ("hopefully", "no timeline"). Responses on Versova and competition were defensive but specific.
